source.snippet: I bought a VPS for hosting my node.js backend. I disabled root password login, created a user with sudo and a user called deploy. A github action builds docker image from repo and uses ssh to login as deploy user and start the container. In a folder there is a docker compose and .env. The env is passed to the compose. Ssh key is in action secrets... Someone compromised my resend api key. I am learning devops now so I used AI a lot.

problem_statement: Solo developers and small teams self-hosting backends on VPS expose API keys and secrets via .env files in docker-compose setups, leading to credential compromise. They lack accessible, opinionated secrets-management tooling that fits a simple VPS+GitHub Actions workflow.
target_segment: Indie developers and small dev teams self-hosting Node.js or containerised backends on VPS, using GitHub Actions CI/CD
notes: Buyer context: person paying for VPS + using production infrastructure (Grafana, Loki, Prometheus stack mentioned). Paid tools like Doppler ($10-$30/mo) and Infisical exist, suggesting willingness to pay in this segment. Signal is single instance but the problem class (leaked .env secrets in docker-compose on VPS) is extremely common and well-documented across ServerFault, Reddit r/devops, and similar. Prioritised over weaker signals in this batch.
